'''Balajapalli Sriram Shastry''' (born 26 November 1950 in [[Akola]], India)<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is an Indian-American condensed matter physicist, specializing in strongly-correlated Fermi systems, [[quantum integrable system]]s,<ref name="iasfellows">{{cite web|title=Dr. B Srisram Shastry|website=Fellows' portal, Indian Academy of Sciences, Bengaluru|url=https://fellows.ias.ac.in/profile/v/FL1988022}}</ref> and statistical mechanics.<ref name="insaindia">{{cite web|title=Indian Fellow, Balajapalli Sriram Shastry|website=Indian National Science Academy|url=https://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N99-1260}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sriram Shastry|website=Physics Department, University of California, Santa Cruz|url=http://physics.ucsc.edu/~sriram/sriram.html}} (links for all of Shastry's publications)</ref>

==Biography==
B. Sriram Shastry graduated in 1968 with a B.Sc. from [[Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University|Nagpur University]] and in 1970 with an M.Sc. in physics from [[Indian Institute of Technology Madras]] (IIT Madras). He received his Ph.D. in 1976 from [[Mumbai]]'s [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (T.I.F.R.),<ref name=aps>{{cite web|website=American Physical Society|title=2009 Lars Onsager Prize Recipient, B. Sriram Shastry|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Shastry&first_nm=B.&year=2009}}</ref> where he worked with [[Chanchal Kumar Majumdar]].<ref name=insaindia/> Shastry's doctoral dissertation, entitled ''Studies in the Magnetic Properties of C.P.C. and Nickel'',<ref>{{cite web|title=Ph.D.'s from DTP (1970 onwards)|website=Theses and past students, Department of Theoretical Physics (DPT), Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)|url=https://theory.tifr.res.in/Research/Thesis/list-phd.pdf}}</ref> dealt with "itinerant magnetism and quantum systems in low dimensions".<ref name=aps/> After completing his Ph.D., he was a lecturer in physics at the [[University of Hyderabad]]. As a postdoc he worked in 1979 at [[Imperial College, London]]<ref name=insaindia/> and from 1980 to 1982 at the University of Utah, where he worked with [[T. Bill Sutherland]] on solvable models. From 1982 to 1987 Shastry worked in India at T.I.F.R. on magnetism of metals and the integrability of the 1-dimensional [[Hubbard model]]. At Princeton University he was a visiting faculty member from 1987 to 1988 and from 2000 to 2001. At [[Bell Laboratories]] from 1988 to 1994 his research included [[Relaxation (NMR)|nuclear magnetic relaxation]] and [[Raman scattering]] in [[High-temperature superconductivity|high-''T''<sub>c</sub> systems]]. From 1994 to 2003 at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (I.I.Sc.), he was a professor working on [[spin ice]] and superconductivity from repulsive models. Since 2003 he is a professor at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]].<ref name=aps/><ref name=insaindia/>

B. Sriram Shastry was elected in 1988 a Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]],<ref name=iasfellows/> in 1999 a Fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]],<ref name=insaindia/> in 2000 a Fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS),<ref name=twas>{{cite web|title=Fellow: Shastry, B. Sriram|website=TWAS Directory, The World Academy of Sciences|url=https://twas.org/directory/shastry-b-sriram}}</ref> and in 2006 a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. He is a Fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]].<ref name=aps/> He received the 1998 TWAS award in physics.<ref name=twas/> In 2009 he received the [[Lars Onsager Prize]] for "pioneering work in developing and solving models of strongly correlated systems and for wide-ranging contributions to phenomenological many-body theory, which have advanced the analysis of experiments on strongly correlated materials."<ref name=aps/> Since 2011 he is on the scientific advisory board of the Max Planck Institute for Complex Systems in Dresden.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}

He is married and has two sons.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}
